title: Sex without crossovers mimics clonal reproduction in Rhynchospora tenuis.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: ENA (European Nucleotide Archive) file report for PRJEB98016: 242 raw-read runs (146 Illumina WGS, i.e. whole-genome sequencing; 56 ChIP-Seq; 14 Hi-C; 12 PacBio WGS; 8 ATAC-seq; 4 snRNA-seq; 2 bisulfite) and 0 analysis objects. NCBI BioProject search found 5 R. tenuis projects. Zenodo DOI/species search found nothing from this paper. The paper is not in Europe PMC (no PMCID), so there was no supplement to list.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the bioRxiv preprint: 9 accessions (18 haplotypes) assembled; 10,997 genotyped pollen grains; 49 and 62 F1 (first-generation offspring) plants from two self-crosses; processed tracks said to be on EDMOND, the Max Planck data repository (not opened); 'all other data available from the corresponding author upon request'.

a1_downloadable.note: Raw reads are public in ENA PRJEB98016 (checked). Processed genotype tables are said to be on EDMOND but I did not open them; the rest is 'on request'.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: There is no outcome table. Any label (pollen genotype, transmission bias, haplotype) would have to be built from raw reads by alignment and genotype calling. The paper is descriptive, not a set of measured outcomes across many items.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are raw FASTQ (sequencing read) files only; ENA lists no processed analysis objects.

a4_units_stated.note: No tabular measurement exists to carry units.

a5_enough_rows.note: One species and 9 accessions; the unit of interest (genome or cross) numbers in single digits. The 10,997 pollen genotypes come from the paper text only and carry no prediction target.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Hundreds of GB of raw reads (not summed); a single ChIP run is ~0.3 GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Building genotypes needs alignment pipelines that do not fit the laptop budget.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 242 runs in ENA is consistent with the assays the paper describes; no count conflict found.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists; any genotype would be the output of a variant-calling pipeline, not a direct measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No well-defined prediction task: this is a single-species cytogenetics and genomics study with no table of labelled outcomes.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use single-pollen-grain genotypes to predict which chromosome versions get passed on more often.
plain_idea.train_on: Genotypes of individual pollen grains (10,997 reported in the paper, not verified) that would have to be called from raw reads.
plain_idea.predict: How often each haplotype (each parental version of a chromosome) is transmitted. It comes from counting genotypes, so it is a summary statistic, not a per-item label.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Of interest to people who study meiosis evolution, but it is a counting analysis that the paper already did, not an ML problem.

ml_idea: None viable. The data is raw sequencing of one plant species, and the findings (no crossovers, biased transmission) come from counts that need no model.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: rejected at Part A before any feature table could be defined.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: ENA file report shows only raw reads and no processed tables (done; this killed it).

verdict_reason: Fails A2/A3/A5: ENA holds only 242 raw-read runs from one species, with no outcome table, and the paper's findings come from counting rather than prediction.
